issues.reason: Names and casing states that string literals are double-quoted "preserving surface form" (and the Dr-Okoro title precedent keeps the abbreviated surface in the Name string), so the literal must be "Tenn.", the run of characters the text actually shows.

Abbreviation expansion is uncovered territory the reviewer's own gap 1 concedes, and (From frist tennessee) is well-typed (From is the licensed entity-attached surface preposition) and true of the standard reading of "R-Tenn." — "the senator from Tennessee" — so the calibration line protects it as graceful improvisation.

"Point at the words" is satisfied — the "R-" of "R-Tenn." is what puts (Member frist republican) there, decompressing a notation rather than importing an unstated relation, and the Past wrapper is exactly the appositive rule ("past host -> (Past (Member halvard wheelwright))").

A finite clausal complement of an adjective is gap territory (reviewer's gap 4), and Theme carrying a sealed proposition is the instruction set's own attitude machinery ("attaches the complement proposition P by Theme") applied to a reified state witness — nothing false, ill-typed, or asserted at top level.

an adjective taking a finite clausal complement ("confident (that) we're going to have a bill")
